1.title: France's smallest yet most distinctive wine region
1.html:
Alsace covers only 8,280 km² (190 km long, 50 km wide, 1.5% of mainland France), making it the smallest administrative region of mainland France — slightly smaller than Corsica (8,680 km²).

📍 Latitude: 47°50′ to 49°N, almost at the northern limit of viable viticulture.
🌡️ The advantage of slow ripening: Because the region lies far north and the growing season is cool, grapes ripen slowly and fully preserve their natural aromatic compounds, giving Alsace whites both delicacy and freshness.

Geographically, Alsace lies in the northeast corner of France, bordering Germany to the east and north; the vineyards run along the eastern and southern foothills of the Vosges massif (Massif Vosgien), out to the edge of the Rhine alluvial plain.
2.title: Six Distinctive Traits of Alsace
2.items.0.label: Named After Grapes
2.items.0.desc: Most French AOCs are named after places, but Alsace traditionally names its wines after grape varieties — a special case in France
2.items.1.label: Almost All White
2.items.1.desc: Apart from Pinot Noir, almost no red is made; even Pinot Noir was traditionally made into rosé, with quality red only in excellent vintages
2.items.2.label: The Vin du Rhin Bottle
2.items.2.desc: Regulations require the slender "Rhine bottle" (flûte) — one of the few French regions with a mandatory bottle shape
2.items.3.label: Three-Tier AOC Structure
2.items.3.desc: Alsace → Alsace + geographical denomination → Alsace Grand Cru: a step-by-step classification logic
2.items.4.label: French–German Cultural Blend
2.items.4.desc: The region changed hands between France and Germany many times; its grape varieties and winemaking traditions are deeply influenced by the German Rhine
2.items.5.label: 10 Varieties, 13 Terroirs
2.items.5.desc: A small region that holds remarkable diversity of grape varieties and geology

3.html:

Total vineyard area is about 15,570 hectares (2009), farmed by about 4,700 growers; 1,820 of them (holding 2 hectares or more) account for 90% of the planted area — showing an industry dominated by small and medium family estates.
4.question: Alsace's vineyards lie far north with a cool climate. What benefit does this bring to wine style?
4.options.0: Grapes cannot ripen, so only sparkling wine can be made
4.options.1: Slow ripening preserves the grapes' natural aromatic compounds, giving delicacy and freshness
4.options.2: The cool climate makes sugar levels especially high
4.options.3: No obvious benefit; it is purely a historical accident
4.explanation: Alsace's latitude (47°50′–49°N) lies almost at the northern limit of viticulture. This is exactly why grapes ripen slowly and preserve their natural aromatics, creating the signature Alsace style of delicate aromas together with fresh acidity.
5.message: Alsace overview complete! You now have the core picture of France's most distinctive white wine region.
